hero.headline: BRONZE FOR THEM. GOLD FOR HIM?
hero.standfirst: Nobody dreams of the third-place match — but tonight's has a trophy hidden inside it. Mbappé sits level with Messi on eight goals, and while Messi must wait for tomorrow's final, Mbappé gets first strike in Miami. Around him, two bruised teams pick through their squads: Saliba is likely out for France, Rice is not expected to start for England, and Kobbie Mainoo may finally get his first World Cup minutes.
hero.photoCaption: Kylian Mbappé — eight goals, one game left, and first swing at the Golden Boot tonight

briefing.text: Team news: Saliba's first-half injury against Spain likely rules him out — Lacroix is favourite to step in. England may hand debuts and rest Rice, with James also a doubt.
The Crystal Ball says France 2–1 tonight — and returns tomorrow morning with its final-day call for Spain–Argentina. Record: 5 from 9, two exact scores.
Tomorrow at MetLife, 21:00 our time: the final. The money keeps climbing — $1.66m on Kalshi, split Spain 43, Tie 32, Argentina 28.

todayTitle: TONIGHT: THE BRONZE — THEN THE GOLD
todaySub: France–England in Miami tonight, Spain–Argentina at MetLife tomorrow

today.preview: Two bruised heavyweights and one live prize. France are without Saliba and full of players with a point to prove after the Spain silencing; England weigh how much to rotate, with Rice not expected to start, James a doubt, and Mainoo pushing for a debut. Kane, Bellingham and Saka are all expected to feature — Tuchel does not do dead rubbers. And above it all: Mbappé, level on 8 with Messi, striking first. The market says France, 52 to 25.

keyMan.name: Kylian Mbappé
keyMan.line: Held without a shot on target by Spain, handed one more night by the calendar. The Golden Boot is decided across two evenings — and he bats first.

factors.label: FORM
factors.text: France were perfect until Spain suffocated them; England were unbeaten until the 92nd minute on Wednesday. The difference: France's front line is fit and furious, England's legs did 120 minutes twice this month.

factors.label: HEAD-TO-HEAD
factors.text: The last two tournament meetings both went France's way by 2–1 — Euro 2004 with Zidane's late double, Qatar 2022 with Kane's missed penalty. England's last win in this fixture at a World Cup was 1966.

factors.label: FITNESS & FATIGUE
factors.text: Saliba is likely out for France with Lacroix ready; England expect to rest Rice, have a doubt over James, and may debut Mainoo. Rotation cuts both ways — but England's is deeper.

factors.label: WHERE THE MONEY IS
factors.text: Kalshi's $1.17m leans hard French: 52 against 25 for England, 25 the draw. Note: a drawn third-place match goes straight to penalties — a quarter of the money expects exactly that.

prediction.verdict: France 2–1, and Mbappé finally beats a goalkeeper again — third-place games open up, and his four days of frustration need somewhere to go. England score, the kids impress, but the bronze goes to France.

today.venue: MetLife Stadium, New York / New Jersey
today.preview: One more sleep. Spain's 37-game unbeaten run and record defence against Argentina's 13-game World Cup streak and stoppage-time sorcery. Yamal's hamstring is being managed; Argentina are at full strength. The money has settled: Spain 43, the tie 32, Argentina 28 — $1.66m and climbing. The Crystal Ball's final call lands tomorrow morning, alongside everything you need for the last day of the tournament.
